message.content:
**Freezing point of water at 10 kPa**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), the freezing (melting) point of pure water drops to roughly **–2.2 °C**.  

This value comes from the water phase diagram: as pressure decreases below atmospheric pressure, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) becomes slightly lower. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about 2 °C below the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm.
